summary.plain: On 2 March 1995 the D0 experiment at Fermilab's Tevatron and the CDF experiment announced the top quark together. D0's paper reports 17 events against an expected background of 3.8, concludes that D0 has observed the top quark, and measures its mass and production rate.
summary.technical: D0 search for the Standard Model top quark in pp̄ collisions at √s=1.8 TeV, integrated luminosity about 50 pb⁻¹, in the dilepton and single-lepton channels with and without b-quark tagging: 17 events observed against an expected background of 3.8 ± 0.6 events; probability of an upward background fluctuation 2.0×10⁻⁶ (equivalent to 4.6 standard deviations). The paper concludes "we have observed the top quark" and measures its mass as 199 +19/−21 (stat) ± 22 (syst) GeV/c² and its production cross section as 6.4 ± 2.2 pb.

title: Observation of the Top Quark
why_it_matters: Fermilab's Tevatron page describes the top quark as the last undiscovered quark of the six predicted to exist by current scientific theory; CDF and D0 announced their observations together on 2 March 1995, and D0's paper measures the top quark's mass and production cross section from the same data.
